**2B.9 Research Note: Vladimir Putin in 2024**

Bottom line: the 2024 record is **strongly against** accountability. I found only one weak procedural-safety decree, but the dominant evidence shows no acceptance of responsibility for civilian harm, torture, illegal conduct, or later evidence undermining the war’s stated justification.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Slightly for 2B.9, but indirect | `Указ Президента Российской Федерации от 01.03.2024 г. № 162` | Kremlin | 2024-03-01 | https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/50378/print | Putin amended military statutes to require commanders to prevent crimes and incidents, report problems promptly, respond to weapons-storage alarms, and specify actions for nuclear, chemical, and biological attack scenarios. This is the only 2024 item that weakly points toward discipline and incident prevention, but it is not acceptance of responsibility for failures or abuses. | 2B.9 |
| Against 2B.9 | `UN says Russia continues to torture, execute Ukrainian POWs` | United Nations in Ukraine | 2024-03-26 | https://ukraine.un.org/en/264368-un-says-russia-continues-torture-execute-ukrainian-pows | The UN human rights mission said almost every interviewed POW described torture, with more than half reporting sexual violence. This is direct evidence against accountability for illegal conduct and prisoner abuse. | 2B.9, 2B.4 |
| Against 2B.9 | `Ukraine human rights situation remains bleak three years after Russia’s full-scale armed ...` | United Nations in Ukraine | 2024-12-31 | https://ukraine.un.org/en/286771-ukraine-human-rights-situation-remains-bleak-three-years-after-russia%E2%80%99s-full-scale-armed | The UN said the situation remained bleak, with rising civilian casualties, continued executions and torture of POWs, and efforts to entrench control in occupied territory. That is strong late-year evidence that Putin did not accept responsibility for civilian harm or unlawful conduct. | 2B.9, 2B.4 |
| Against 2B.9 | `Exclusive: Putin-controlled aircraft deported Ukrainian children, US-backed research alleges` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-12-03 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/exclusiveputincontrolled-aircraft-deported-ukrainian-children-usbacked-research-alleges-3750835 | Reuters reported Yale researchers’ allegation that Russian presidential aircraft and funds were used in a child-transfer program. This is an allegation, not a judicial finding, but if accurate it points strongly against accountability for foreseeable unlawful conduct. | 2B.9, 2B.4, 2B.5 |
| Against 2B.9 | `Russia to practice tactical nuclear weapon scenario to deter West` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-05-06 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-to-practice-tactical-nuclear-weapon-scenario-to-deter-west--defence-ministry-3419973 | Russia announced tactical nuclear deployment drills after claiming Western threats. This reflects a coercive posture rather than accountability for escalation or later contradiction of the war rationale. | 2B.9, 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.5 |
| Against 2B.9 | `Russia begins second stage of tactical nuclear weapon drills with Belarus` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-06-11 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-begins-second-stage-of-tactical-nuclear-weapon-drills-with-belarus-3478894 | The Belarus drill phase expanded readiness and cross-border operationalization. It shows sustained escalation and alliance leverage, not accountability for harmful or destabilizing conduct. | 2B.9, 1B.5, 2B.5 |
| Against 2B.9 | `Russia will change nuclear doctrine because of Western role in Ukraine` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-09-01 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-will-change-nuclear-doctrine-due-to-wests-actions-in-ukraine-official-says-3596699 | Moscow justified the doctrine revision as a response to Western involvement in Ukraine. That is evidence against accountability for the earlier justification of conflict; it shows continued blame-shifting and escalation framing instead of correction. | 2B.9, 2B.6, 2B.7 |

**Synthesis**

- Best-supported conclusion: **No**. Putin did not accept accountability for military failures, civilian harm, illegal conduct, or later evidence contradicting the war’s justification.
- The strongest evidence comes from **UN reporting** on torture, executions, and civilian casualties, plus the **child-transfer allegation**.
- The only pro-side item is a **broad discipline decree**; it does not amount to taking responsibility for atrocities or changing course.
- Search gap: I did **not** find a credible 2024 example of Putin acknowledging wrongdoing, apologizing, punishing senior leadership for civilian harm, or revising the conflict narrative in light of contradictory evidence.
